newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's English approves cardiac service for S.Island.
newsitem.headline: NZ's English approves cardiac service for S.Island.

text.p: New Zealand Health Minister Bill English on Friday approved a proposal to develop a new cardiac service for the whole of the South Island.
"Canterbury Health, HealthCare Otago and the surgeons have agreed to set up a joint venture board," English said in a statement.
"The joint venture will oversee and manage the service in the two public hospital sites, Dunedin Hospital and Christhurch Hospital," he said.

A decision on a Christchurch cardiac unit has been on hold since before the October 1996 general election and has caused a split between English and his associate minister, New Zealand First's Neil Kirton.
Kirton had opposed plans for private sector involvement in the unit.
English said it would be up to the three parties to the new joint venture -- the surgeons, Canterbury Health and HealthCare Otago -- to resolve outstanding "issues of detail".
They had said they would be able to do that by June 20, he said.
"We will then have a clear idea of the actual date that the service can commence."
English said the important aspect of the deal he had announced was that it brought to an end the bickering over South Island cardiac services.
"There's never been any question that there would be a public service and that it would include treating patients at Christchurch Hospital.
"My job has been to put together a viable service for the South Island which is going to stick."
